scenario.title: Check In Agreement
scenario.premise: They set a limited check-in plan while the relationship pause continues.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Would one brief check-in halfway through the break feel useful?

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Yes, as long as it is only to confirm we are okay, not to reopen everything.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That is what I mean. A simple message on Sunday.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can do that and keep the rest of the pause intact.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: This brief check-in does not end the pause; the space still matters.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I understand. Can we confirm what this pause is meant to give us?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It is time to think clearly without continuing the same conflict.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: And it is not a final decision about the relationship today.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Correct. We are pausing contact, not deciding the outcome yet.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: When should the pause begin so the boundary is unambiguous?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It should begin after this conversation and the essential details are settled.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: How long should we leave before the first review?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Two weeks feels long enough to reflect without making the pause indefinite.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would a review after two weeks mean we must decide then?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: No, it means we check whether we need more time or can talk calmly.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I appreciate that distinction. How should we record the review time?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We can put one neutral reminder on our calendars and leave it there.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Once it is recorded, I will not send reminders during the pause.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Thank you. One agreed reminder is enough and protects the quiet.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should ordinary updates wait until the review conversation?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, casual updates would blur the no-contact space we are creating.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What about messages that only say I am thinking of you?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Those should wait too, because they still ask the other person to respond emotionally.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I understand. Should we mute the existing chat rather than delete it?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Muting is enough for me, and it avoids making a dramatic gesture.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would seeing read status create pressure during the pause?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It might, so I will not open nonessential messages if one arrives by mistake.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: If I send something accidentally, I will not follow it with explanations.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That helps. We can let an accidental message sit without restarting contact.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should reactions and shared links count as contact too?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, any direct contact should wait unless it fits an agreed exception.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Then I will avoid every casual channel until the review.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will do the same so the boundary applies equally to both of us.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What situations should count as a genuine exception?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: A safety emergency or a time-sensitive shared obligation, nothing broader.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: How should an urgent message begin so it is easy to recognize?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Start with the practical reason and the deadline, without emotional discussion.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Could an urgent message stay to one question when possible?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, one clear question will reduce the chance of reopening the conflict.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: If no answer is needed, I will say that directly.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Please do. Knowing the expected action will keep the contact contained.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What response time is reasonable for a shared obligation?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Within one day unless the message states an earlier unavoidable deadline.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: And a safety emergency can use the fastest available route.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, safety comes before the pause, but ordinary worry does not become an emergency.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That limit feels clear enough for me to follow.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It feels clear to me too, which makes the pause more respectful.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: We still have one shared bill due during the pause. How should we handle it?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will pay my usual share and send only the payment confirmation.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should I acknowledge the confirmation or leave it unanswered?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: A brief received message is fine because it closes the practical task.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: There is also a delivery addressed to you at my place.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Please leave it with the building desk, and I will collect it without meeting.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can do that and send the collection window only once.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Thank you. I will not use the pickup as a reason to start a conversation.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Do we need to exchange any keys during the pause?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: No, we can leave the keys untouched until the review unless access becomes necessary.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That avoids turning a temporary boundary into a final gesture.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Exactly. We should not make irreversible choices while we are still reflecting.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I will keep practical contact limited to what we named.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: And I will not add personal questions to those practical messages.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What should we tell mutual friends if they ask about us?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We can say we are taking private space and do not want messages carried between us.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should we ask them not to give either of us updates?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, indirect updates would undermine the pause even without direct contact.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: There is a group event before our review date. Do you plan to attend?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will skip this one so neither of us has to manage an unexpected meeting.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Thank you. I can attend without wondering whether contact is expected.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That is the goal. The pause should reduce uncertainty, not create a public test.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: If another event appears, should the person invited first decide?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Let us handle each event by practical need and avoid competing for space.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: We can ask a neutral organizer about timing if necessary.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, but only for logistics and not for information about each other.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I will not ask friends to interpret what you are feeling.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will not do that either. Reflection needs to remain our own work.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would checking each other's public updates violate the spirit of the pause?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: For me it would, because it keeps attention fixed without real consent.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can hide updates temporarily instead of reading into them.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will do the same and avoid posting anything aimed at getting a reaction.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should we avoid vague messages that mutual friends might relay?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, indirect signals can create the same pressure as direct contact.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I will speak to my own support people without asking them to choose sides.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That is healthy, and I will keep my support conversations private too.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What if one of us feels a strong urge to break the pause?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Write the thought privately, wait a day, and check whether it fits an exception.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: If it does not fit, it stays unsent until the review.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes. An intense feeling does not require immediate contact.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That gives us a concrete way to respect the boundary.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It also gives the feeling time to become clearer before we discuss it.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What do you hope to understand during these two weeks?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I want to understand my needs without arguing against yours in my head.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I want to notice which concerns are patterns and which came from one hard week.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That distinction could make our review more honest and specific.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should we each write down what would need to change?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, but as personal notes, not a list of demands sent during the pause.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I will include what I can change, not only what I want from you.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will do the same so responsibility does not travel in one direction.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would outside support be appropriate while we reflect?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, as long as support does not become a campaign to pressure the other person.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can ask for perspective while keeping the decision ours.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That feels respectful and keeps the pause focused on clarity.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I will not treat silence as evidence for any conclusion.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Neither will I. Silence is the agreed boundary, not an answer.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: How should we begin the review conversation when the time comes?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We can each share what we learned before discussing possible next steps.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Before we wrap up, can we return to what we said earlier?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, I have one more thought about it.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will respect the break we agreed on until our review, without treating the silence as a final answer.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: We will keep the check-in brief.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Agreed.
